key_insight: Training an LLM to use feedback across successive molecular edits improved multi-objective optimization while preserving similarity to the starting molecule.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support early-stage therapeutic discovery, but the abstract provides no cancer-specific or clinical validation.
method: Use reinforcement learning to train GeLLM³O for multi-turn molecular optimization.
Track property improvements and source-molecule similarity in a feedback vector.
Align rewards with feedback to encourage progressive improvement across turns.
evidence_signal: Across 10 multi-objective optimization tasks, GeLLM³O-MFG achieved an average similarity-constrained success rate of 81.50%, versus 70.81% for the base model.
watch_item: Computational optimization success does not establish experimental activity, safety, or therapeutic benefit.
paper_title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization
